session.question: How did broiler chicks in Iraq compare in maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease vaccination, and which strain performed better in the study?
session.answer:
In Iraqi 1-day-old imported broiler chicks, maternal derived antibodies (MDA) against Newcastle disease were high in both Cobb 500 and Ross 308 strains, as measured by indirect ELISA. Cobb 500 chicks showed 100% positivity for maternal antibody titers, compared with 97.78% in Ross 308, indicating slightly better seropositivity in Cobb 500. Cobb 500 also had a higher mean maternal antibody titer (9,871.47 versus 8,647.76), a lower coefficient of variation (12.41% versus 15.18%), and a higher mean vaccination index (966.59 versus 821.60), suggesting more uniform and more protective inherited immunity. (ezzulddin2022theabilityto chunk 1)

Overall, both strains had high and fairly uniform maternal titers, but Cobb 500 performed better than Ross 308 in terms of antibody level, consistency, and predicted protection against Newcastle disease vaccination. (ezzulddin2022theabilityto chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-6bc09052: The study compared maternal derived antibodies (MDA) against Newcastle disease in 1-day-old imported broiler chicks from two strains in Mosul governorate, Iraq: Cobb 500 and Ross 308. Seven hundred and seven blood samples were tested by indirect ELISA. Cobb 500 chicks showed better results overall: 100% positivity for maternal antibody titers versus 97.78% in Ross 308, a higher mean maternal antibody titer (9,871.47 vs 8,647.76), lower CV (12.41% vs 15.18%), and a higher mean vaccination index (966.59 vs 821.60). The conclusion was that both strains had high, uniform maternal titers, but Cobb 500 produced higher protective titers than Ross 308.
From Thamer Abdulazeez Ezzulddin, Dhyaa Mohammad Taher Jwher, and Akeel Mohammad Shareef. The ability to resist newcastle disease through inherited immunity in different strains of broilers in nineveh governorate. Open Veterinary Journal, 2022. URL: https://doi.org/10.5455/ovj.2022.v12.i6.20, doi:10.5455/ovj.2022.v12.i6.20.

pqac-55f0f5e3: The study compared maternal derived antibodies against Newcastle disease (ND) in 1-day-old imported broiler chicks in Nineveh/Mosul governorate, focusing on Cobb 500 and Ross 308 strains. Seven hundred and seven blood samples from 28 Ross 308 flocks and 17 Cobb 500 flocks were tested by indirect ELISA. Results showed Cobb 500 chicks had better maternal antibody protection: 100% positivity vs 97.78% in Ross 308, a higher mean maternal antibody titer (9,871.47 vs 8,647.76), lower CV variability (12.41% vs 15.18%), and a higher vaccination index (966.59 vs 821.60). The conclusion was that both strains had high and fairly uniform titers, but Cobb 500 produced more protective titers than Ross 308.
